steps.phase: Read the frozen brief and surface assumptions
steps.title: Preserve the exact frozen problem brief
steps.content: FROZEN BRIEF — ID: mlops_011. Title: ‘Design a Data Pipeline for ML with Data Quality Gates’. Slug: ‘design-a-data-pipeline-for-ml-with-data-quality-gates’. Description: ‘Design a data pipeline that processes raw data into ML-ready datasets with automated data validation, quality gates, schema enforcement, and data versioning.’ Difficulty: Medium. Category: MLOps - Data Pipeline. Domain: aiml. Estimated time: 45-60 minutes. Requirements: ‘Ingest data from multiple sources (databases, APIs, files)’; ‘Validate data quality at each pipeline stage’; ‘Enforce schema consistency and evolution’; ‘Detect data anomalies and completeness issues’; ‘Version datasets for reproducibility’; ‘Transform data into ML-ready feature tables’; ‘Generate data quality reports’; ‘Alert on data quality failures before training’. Constraints: ‘Pipeline completion within 2 hours for daily runs’; ‘Data quality check latency under 5 minutes’; ‘Handle 1TB+ daily data volume’; ‘Support schema evolution without breaking pipelines’; ‘99.9% pipeline reliability’. Hints: ‘Use Great Expectations or Pandera for data validation’; ‘Implement DVC or LakeFS for data versioning’; ‘Use Apache Spark or dbt for data transformations’; ‘Implement circuit breakers for bad data prevention’; ‘Use data contracts between producers and consumers’; ‘Implement data lineage tracking with OpenLineage’. Tags: mlops, data-pipeline, data-quality, data-validation, data-versioning, etl. Companies: Airbnb, Netflix, Uber, Spotify. Hints are candidate techniques, not additional requirements; this structural draft does not claim any target has been achieved.

steps.phase: Read the frozen brief and surface assumptions
steps.title: Separate the brief from sizing and policy assumptions
steps.content: FACT — The brief specifies daily runs completing within two hours, quality checks under five minutes, 1TB+ daily input, schema evolution, and 99.9% pipeline reliability. ASSUMPTION / OPEN QUESTIONS — Confirm source count and change rates, file/object sizes, arrival windows, late data, partition keys, freshness semantics, validation sampling policy, downstream feature-store contract, recovery objectives, and which portion of the daily run is inside the two-hour clock. The diagram is not evidence that these objectives are met; test the full measured workload.

steps.phase: Place ingestion, contract, and processing components
steps.title: Represent database producers
steps.content: Read database data through bounded snapshots or incremental change capture, using a source cursor or watermark to make retries resumable. The required source-specific consistency model is not stated in the brief.

component.label: Operational Database Sources
component.description: Structured producer data ingested by snapshot or incremental reads.
component.highlightReason: The existing Database catalog type represents one of the named source families.

properties.purpose: Expose structured records through bounded snapshots or incremental extraction with resumable source watermarks.

steps.phase: Place ingestion, contract, and processing components
steps.title: Represent API producers
steps.content: Use a validated API boundary for producer integrations, pagination, authentication, and source-specific rate handling. A source API error should not silently mark an incomplete daily partition as complete.

component.label: Producer API Connectors
component.description: Validated integration boundary for upstream API data.
component.highlightReason: The catalog API Gateway supplies a canonical entry point for API producer integration.

properties.purpose: Authenticate producer integrations, validate payload envelopes, and manage pagination and rate responses for API data ingestion.

steps.phase: Place ingestion, contract, and processing components
steps.title: Represent file producers and landing objects
steps.content: Land source files with checksums and producer metadata so duplicate delivery and partial upload can be detected before processing.

component.label: File Landing Zone
component.description: Incoming file objects with source and integrity metadata.
component.highlightReason: The existing Object Storage type represents file ingestion and avoids loading large files into API requests.

properties.purpose: Accept incoming source files with checksums, arrival timestamps, source identity, and completeness markers before batch processing.

steps.phase: Place ingestion, contract, and processing components
steps.title: Add durable ingestion work coordination
steps.content: Represent source manifests and partitions as durable work items. Retry failed work idempotently and retain a dead-letter or quarantine path for source records that cannot be safely interpreted.

component.label: Ingestion Work Queue
component.description: Durable source-partition work and bounded retry coordination.
component.highlightReason: The catalog Queue type is reusable for scheduled and incremental ingestion work.

properties.purpose: Queue source manifests and partition jobs with idempotent retry, bounded backoff, and a quarantine path for invalid work.

steps.phase: Place ingestion, contract, and processing components
steps.title: Add daily pipeline orchestration
steps.content: Coordinate source readiness, partition processing, validation gates, output publication, lineage completion, and failure notifications. Do not publish downstream-ready state until required stages and completeness checks succeed.

component.label: Daily Data Pipeline Orchestrator
component.description: Schedules, coordinates, retries, and gates data pipeline stages.
component.highlightReason: The MLOps Pipeline catalog type models staged orchestration without adding a new component.

properties.purpose: Coordinate daily and incremental DAG runs, source readiness, idempotent partition retries, quality gates, dataset publication, and training release decisions.

steps.phase: Place ingestion, contract, and processing components
steps.title: Represent versioned producer and consumer contracts
steps.content: Store schema and semantic contracts with compatibility policy and ownership. Review breaking changes explicitly and allow a controlled migration path rather than silently accepting incompatible columns.

component.label: Data Contracts & Schema Policy
component.description: Versioned producer-consumer schemas and compatibility rules.
component.highlightReason: Configuration Management is the current catalog type for version-controlled contract policy.

properties.purpose: Version data contracts, field semantics, ownership, and compatibility rules; require reviewed migration for breaking schema evolution.

steps.phase: Place ingestion, contract, and processing components
steps.title: Add stage-by-stage validation and transforms
steps.content: Run contract checks, completeness and anomaly checks, transformations, and stage-level quality gates. Great Expectations or Pandera and Spark or dbt are possible implementations from the hints, not required products. Isolate bad partitions so a circuit breaker can stop unsafe publication without discarding good source evidence.

component.label: Validation & Transformation Workers
component.description: Contract-aware processing and quality checks at each pipeline stage.
component.highlightReason: The existing Processing Worker type covers scalable batch validation and transformation.

properties.purpose: Apply source and stage contracts, schema compatibility checks, completeness and anomaly tests, and repeatable transformations; quarantine failing partitions before publication.

steps.phase: Place ingestion, contract, and processing components
steps.title: Add versioned raw and curated dataset storage
steps.content: Keep immutable raw inputs and curated dataset snapshots addressable by manifest, source watermark, schema version, and transformation revision. DVC or LakeFS are candidate approaches from the hint list; the design does not require either vendor.

component.label: Versioned Raw & Curated Datasets
component.description: Immutable raw partitions and published dataset revisions.
component.highlightReason: The existing Object Storage type fits large immutable dataset artifacts and snapshots.

properties.purpose: Retain immutable raw inputs and curated snapshots with manifests pinning source watermarks, schema versions, transformation revisions, and checksums.

steps.phase: Place ingestion, contract, and processing components
steps.title: Persist run and lineage metadata
steps.content: Record pipeline run identity, input partitions, contract revision, code/config version, validation results, output manifest, and lineage events so a dataset can be reproduced and audited.

component.label: Pipeline Run & Lineage Metadata
component.description: Queryable run state, validation results, and dataset lineage references.
component.highlightReason: The existing Database type stores compact lineage and run metadata separately from bulk data.

properties.purpose: Index pipeline runs, source watermarks, contract revisions, validation outcomes, lineage references, and immutable dataset manifest IDs.

steps.phase: Place ingestion, contract, and processing components
steps.title: Add quality reporting and analytical tables
steps.content: Materialize quality summaries and consumer-facing analytical tables separately from immutable raw evidence. Avoid presenting a report as healthy when required source partitions are missing or quarantined.

component.label: Quality Reports & Analytical Tables
component.description: Queryable summaries, quality reports, and downstream analytical views.
component.highlightReason: The Data Warehouse catalog type supports report queries and analytical consumers.

properties.purpose: Store stage-level quality summaries, completeness and anomaly reports, and queryable analytical tables with source and dataset revision references.

steps.phase: Place ingestion, contract, and processing components
steps.title: Publish ML-ready feature tables
steps.content: Publish feature tables only from validated, versioned output. Keep feature definitions and dataset revision references consistent with the consumer's training contract; online-serving semantics are not specified by this batch-pipeline brief.

component.label: ML Feature Tables
component.description: Validated feature datasets prepared for downstream model training.
component.highlightReason: The existing Feature Store type directly represents ML-ready feature tables.

properties.purpose: Publish training-ready feature tables from quality-approved dataset revisions with reproducible feature and source lineage.

steps.phase: Place ingestion, contract, and processing components
steps.title: Add a quality report workspace
steps.content: Give data and ML consumers a view of run state, source completeness, validation failures, anomalies, quarantined partitions, and published dataset versions.

component.label: Data Quality Report Workspace
component.description: Run-level and dataset-level quality reports for operators and consumers.
component.highlightReason: The catalog Web App type provides an operator-facing report surface.

properties.purpose: Display pipeline run status, stage validation reports, completeness and anomaly findings, quarantine details, and published dataset revision lineage.

steps.phase: Place ingestion, contract, and processing components
steps.title: Monitor pipeline health and quality gates
steps.content: Observe stage duration, end-to-end daily completion, source lag, quality-check duration, retries, quarantines, and failure rate. Treat the reliability objective as an SLO to measure rather than a property guaranteed by the diagram.

component.label: Pipeline & Data Quality Monitoring
component.description: Stage metrics, reliability SLOs, quality dashboards, and alert signals.
component.highlightReason: The Monitoring catalog component exposes both pipeline operations and data quality signals.

properties.purpose: Track stage checks, source completeness, anomaly counts, latency, retries, daily pipeline completion, and reliability; expose reports and alert conditions.

steps.phase: Place ingestion, contract, and processing components
steps.title: Alert owners before training consumes bad data
steps.content: Route actionable quality-gate and pipeline-failure notifications to the responsible producer or data owner. Notification delivery is separate from the publication gate: failed quality must also prevent the dataset-ready signal.

component.label: Quality Failure Notifications
component.description: Owner alerts for failed data quality and pipeline stages.
component.highlightReason: The existing Notification Service type handles failure alerts without acting as the quality gate itself.

properties.purpose: Notify dataset and source owners about blocking validation failures, incomplete partitions, schema incompatibility, and pipeline failures before downstream training is released.

steps.phase: Place ingestion, contract, and processing components
steps.title: Represent the gated training consumer
steps.content: Training starts only from an explicitly published feature-table revision whose required quality gates passed. Preserve the data and contract versions in training metadata for reproducibility.

component.label: Downstream Model Training
component.description: Consumes only quality-approved and versioned ML feature tables.
component.highlightReason: The catalog Model Training type makes the pre-training quality gate explicit.

properties.purpose: Start training from a published feature-table revision only after required validation gates pass; retain dataset, contract, and code revision identities.

steps.phase: Choose compatibility, versioning, and failure policies
steps.title: Evolve schemas through reviewed compatibility
steps.content: For additive compatible changes, allow a pinned migration and producer-consumer rollout; for breaking changes, quarantine or reject the affected partition until a reviewed migration is available. Compatibility direction, field deprecation windows, and semantic checks remain owner decisions because the brief does not specify them.

decision.question: How should the pipeline handle a changed source schema?
decision.chosen: Validate against a versioned data contract, accept only approved compatible changes, and isolate breaking or unknown changes from publication.
decision.chosenReason: This supports evolution without allowing an unexpected field change to silently corrupt downstream ML features.

alternatives.option: Coerce every incoming schema to the latest form
alternatives.tradeoff: Implicit coercion can lose semantics and make historical runs irreproducible.

steps.phase: Choose compatibility, versioning, and failure policies
steps.title: Make dataset versions reproducible
steps.content: Identify each published dataset by immutable input manifests, source watermarks, schema/contract revision, transformation code/config, and output checksums. DVC and LakeFS are hinted alternatives, not commitments; choose the mechanism after retention, branching, and access requirements are known.

decision.question: What must a dataset version pin?
decision.chosen: Pin input object revisions, source watermarks, contracts, transform versions, and validation results in a durable manifest.
decision.chosenReason: A version label alone cannot reproduce or audit a derived feature table.

alternatives.tradeoff: This loses the evidence needed to reproduce prior model inputs.

steps.phase: Choose compatibility, versioning, and failure policies
steps.title: Fail closed on quality gates and retry idempotently
steps.content: A failed contract, completeness, or anomaly gate blocks publication and training release. Preserve raw inputs and the failed report, retry only replay-safe stages, and use a circuit breaker to stop repeated unsafe processing. The exact quarantine and owner-override policy needs agreement.

decision.question: Can a partial or failed daily run publish training data?
decision.chosen: No; keep outputs in a non-published state until required checks pass or an explicitly governed exception is recorded.
decision.chosenReason: The brief requires alerts before training when quality fails, so notification alone is not a sufficient control.

alternatives.option: Publish partial output and alert afterward
alternatives.tradeoff: Training could consume known incomplete or invalid data before an owner responds.

steps.phase: Turn supplied pipeline limits into validation gates
steps.title: Validate the daily completion objective
steps.content: Measure from the agreed daily-run start boundary through all required validation and publication gates, including late source arrivals and retries.

scaleTrigger.metric: Pipeline completion within 2 hours for daily runs
scaleTrigger.action: Profile source waits, stage critical paths, and partition skew; parallelize or right-size only where measurement identifies a bottleneck.
scaleTrigger.impact: Keeps the stated end-to-end time budget visible without assuming all sources arrive simultaneously.

steps.phase: Turn supplied pipeline limits into validation gates
steps.title: Validate quality-check latency
steps.content: Define which stage-level check latency the target covers and test at representative data volume and rule complexity; the brief does not state a percentile.

scaleTrigger.metric: Data quality check latency under 5 minutes
scaleTrigger.action: Measure per-check and per-stage duration, then optimize or partition expensive checks while preserving their validation semantics.
scaleTrigger.impact: Avoids hiding a slow check behind an aggregate pipeline duration.

steps.phase: Turn supplied pipeline limits into validation gates
steps.title: Validate daily data volume behavior
steps.content: Exercise ingestion, validation, transformation, lineage, and output publication with representative 1TB+ daily volume, including skew and small-file effects.

scaleTrigger.action: Measure storage throughput, partition sizes, shuffle, and validation cost; tune parallelism from observed resource and skew metrics.
scaleTrigger.impact: Tests the whole data path rather than assuming object storage capacity alone proves throughput.

steps.phase: Turn supplied pipeline limits into validation gates
steps.title: Validate safe schema evolution
steps.content: Test additive, renamed, removed, and type-changed fields against consumer contracts, historical replay, and the explicit migration policy.

scaleTrigger.metric: Support schema evolution without breaking pipelines
scaleTrigger.action: Gate deployment on compatibility fixtures and publish a new contract revision only with an approved migration path.
scaleTrigger.impact: Makes compatibility behavior observable across producers, transforms, and consumers.

steps.phase: Turn supplied pipeline limits into validation gates
steps.title: Measure pipeline reliability
steps.content: Define the reliability numerator, denominator, evaluation window, and treatment of source outages, late data, and authorized reruns before declaring the target satisfied.

scaleTrigger.action: Track successful eligible runs, recoverable retries, terminal failures, and withheld unsafe publications against the agreed SLO definition.
scaleTrigger.impact: Prevents retrying or skipping quality checks from being counted as reliability success.

steps.phase: Review the structural draft
steps.title: Review the architecture and remaining evidence
steps.content: The graph connects database, API, and file sources to durable work coordination; contract-pinned orchestration and validation; immutable raw and curated dataset versions; lineage and reports; approved feature tables; a pre-training quality gate; and owner alerts. FACTS are the frozen brief and its stated targets. ASSUMPTIONS include the daily-run clock boundary, source arrival patterns, compatibility policy, validation percentile, and reliability definition. Structural tests do not prove browser apply/save/reload or live assessment quality; those gates remain pending.
